plain_english: A traveler runs toward mirage water in a desert; if one thing exists despite different forms, possibility is questioned.
sanskrit_cite:
marau marīcikāmbhobhiḥ snānecchur abhidhāvati /
bhinnasvarūpād yady ekam asti vastv iti saṃbhavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.302]

plain_english: Then difference is not ultimate by cause-difference; but if different form is accepted as one, the issue remains.
sanskrit_cite:
tarhi kāraṇabhedena na bhedaḥ pāramārthikaḥ /
atha bhinnasvarūpaṃ tad ekaṃ cety upagamyate // [AgMsv_1.303]

plain_english: Nature-difference would lead to difference; if that is abandoned, the vow is broken. Thus action should not be one agent like wood.
sanskrit_cite:
svabhāvabhedo bhedāyety etat tyaktaṃ vrataṃ bhavet /
nanv itthaṃ sā kriyā mā bhūd ekā kāṣṭhādi kārakam // [AgMsv_1.304]

plain_english: Let fruit be produced even so; there is no harm to us, because action is not another power.
sanskrit_cite:
phalaṃ janayatām evam apy astu na hi naḥ kṣatiḥ /
kriyā hi nāma nāsmākam anyā śaktis tv asau yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.305]

plain_english: Power arises by fruit-piercing arrangement from non-difference of being and self; that power is the lord's, and he is world-self-form.
sanskrit_cite:
śaktiś ca phalabhitkḷptyā bhāvātmaivāvibhedataḥ /
sā ca śaktir vibhor eva sa ca viśvātmavigrahaḥ // [AgMsv_1.306]

plain_english: By fruit and agent difference, power is not ultimately different; even in the lord's undifferentiated self, difference appears.
sanskrit_cite:
phalakārakabhedena na bhinnā paramārthataḥ /
svātmany abhinne 'pi vibhor evaṃ bhedāvabhāsanāt // [AgMsv_1.307]

plain_english: Action-power is called that by which the great lord is agent; but how can bound souls act? Let that be explained.
sanskrit_cite:
kriyāśaktir iti proktā yayā kartā maheśvaraḥ /
nanu yat paśavaḥ kuryuḥ kathaṃ tad upapadyatām // [AgMsv_1.308]

plain_english: They, from having one life in difference, would perform differentiated action; enough of this, how bound souls act is clear.
sanskrit_cite:
te hi bhedaikajīvatvāt kuryur bhedavatīṃ kriyām /
alam etena paśavaḥ kathaṃ kuryur iti sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.309]

plain_english: That self-contradictory statement is like a barren woman's son; agency is never found in a pot-maker.
sanskrit_cite:
sa eva svavacaśchinno vādo vandhyāsutādivat /
na hi kumbhakṛtaḥ kvāpi kadācit kartṛtā bhavet // [AgMsv_1.310]

plain_english: If that is not non-different from the agent called great lord, then what is made by the potter? Is the pot made by the potter?
sanskrit_cite:
yadi nāsau maheśākhyāt kartur avyatirekabhāk /
nanu kiṃ svit kulālena kumbho 'pi kriyate tataḥ // [AgMsv_1.311]

plain_english: If the lord has world-agency, is there no agency in cloth? If so, cloth too is not made by the potter.
sanskrit_cite:
īśasya viśvakartṛtve kiṃ paṭe 'pi na kartṛtā /
yady evaṃ tat kulālena paṭo 'pi kriyate na kim // [AgMsv_1.312]

plain_english: If so, there is no other agent; for auspicious and inauspicious actions, toward whom is causality for producing their own fruit?
sanskrit_cite:
nanv evaṃ sati no kartā ko 'py anya iti karmaṇām /
śubhāśubhānāṃ svaphalaṃ kartuṃ kaṃ prati hetutā // [AgMsv_1.313]

plain_english: Thus it is, venerable one; for those who know thus, no fruit arises anywhere, auspicious or inauspicious.
sanskrit_cite:
evam evaitad āyuṣmaṃs tathāhy evaṃ vijānatām /
na kiṃ cana phalaṃ kvāpi śubhāśubhasamudbhavam // [AgMsv_1.314]

plain_english: Those who do not know thus enjoy; they are unwise. That very thing called action is impurity rooted in ignorance.
sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ ye tu na jānanti bhuñjate te 'vipaścitaḥ /
tad eva karmasaṃjñaṃ tu malam ajñānamūlakam // [AgMsv_1.315]

plain_english: Approving this only, some consider consciousness-only, indeed a non-agent, because agency is impossible.
sanskrit_cite:
etad evānumanyaiva kecit saṃvittimātrakam /
saṃmanyante hy akartāraṃ kartṛtvānupapattitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.316]

plain_english: Consciousness-form is superior; that is called agency. From consciousness-superiority, inertness would be attributed to this.
sanskrit_cite:
citsvarūpādhikaṃ hy asya yat tat kartṛtvam ucyate /
taj jāḍyam arpayed asmai cidādhikyaprasaṅgataḥ // [AgMsv_1.317]

plain_english: Nature's agency in a person is indeed metaphorically called; those departed from the path of logic vainly debate this in the house.
sanskrit_cite:
prakṛteḥ kartṛtā puṃsi nanu nāmopacaryate /
etan nyāyapathāpetair vṛthā jegīyate gṛhe // [AgMsv_1.318]

plain_english: Figurative usage does not reach the real nature of a thing; such a designation may be empty of reality, so it cannot establish real agency.
sanskrit_cite:
upacāro hi no vastutathātvaṃ pratipadyate /
vyapadeśaḥ paraṃ tādṛg vastuśūnyo 'stu tāvatā // [AgMsv_1.319]

plain_english: Even if someone were called fire only figuratively, he would not remove the cold caused by snow, hail, showers, and wind.
sanskrit_cite:
nopacārikavahnitvavyapadeśe 'pi mānavaḥ /
himānīśīkarāsārivātotthaśiśirāpahaḥ // [AgMsv_1.320]

plain_english: Prakṛti is not called the seer of the self, and there is no other candidate left; so there is no one to whom agency could even be figuratively assigned.
sanskrit_cite:
draṣṭuḥ puṃsaś ca na draṣṭrī prakṛtiḥ parigīyate /
na cānyo 'sti varāko 'taḥ kartṛbhāvopacārakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.321]

plain_english: What purpose is served by talk of agency if it is only figurative? Such a designation need not be real and can simply be changed.
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ ca prayojanaṃ tasya kartṛtvavyavahārajam /
vyapadeśas tu nāvastu parivartayituṃ kṣamaḥ // [AgMsv_1.322]

plain_english: Even those who, following their doctrine, accept the self as an agent must first answer this question that we put to them.
sanskrit_cite:
ye 'py ātmānaṃ nayavidaḥ kartāraṃ samupāgaman /
te 'pi praśnam imaṃ tāvad asmākaṃ pratibhārpitam // [AgMsv_1.323]

plain_english: Can the kind of agency known from ordinary action, which involves vibration, really belong to an all-pervading self that has no vibration?
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ yādṛglokasaṃsiddhakartṛtvaṃ karmayogataḥ /
spandātma tad vibhau spandahīne samupapadyate // [AgMsv_1.324]

plain_english: The objection is: knowledge, desire to act, and effort form a triad belonging to the self, and that is what is called agency.
sanskrit_cite:
nanu jñānaṃ cikīrṣā ca yatnaś ceti guṇatrayam /
samavaiti yad atrāsya tat kartṛtvam udāhṛtam // [AgMsv_1.325]

plain_english: This kind of reasoning might deceive the childish, but even children are not without awareness.
sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ bālamatīnāṃ dhīr vipralabhyeta vañcakaiḥ /
dārakā api vā vidyur na saṃvedanavarjitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.326]

plain_english: Knowledge is not agency, since it is present everywhere; and desire and effort too are generally found in everyone, so their mere presence does not amount to agency.
sanskrit_cite:
tatra jñānaṃ na kartṛtvaṃ sarvatrāsty eva tad yataḥ /
icchāyatnāv api prāyaḥ saṃstaḥ sarvasya sarvataḥ // [AgMsv_1.327]

plain_english: A potter distressed by not having a house may know, want, and try, yet still be unable to make a house for himself.
sanskrit_cite:
kumbhakāro gṛhābhāvaparitāpitacetanaḥ /
jānann icchan sayatno 'pi kiṃ kuryān nātmano gṛham // [AgMsv_1.328]

plain_english: The objection says: he does not know how to do it, so he does not want to do it and does not try; then how could he make the house?
sanskrit_cite:
nanu kartuṃ na jānāti tataḥ kartuṃ na cecchati /
tasmāt kartuṃ na yatate tad gṛhaṃ kurutāṃ kathaṃ // [AgMsv_1.329]

plain_english: If knowledge, desire, and effort are qualified by 'to do', what does that qualifier mean? Does it mean having vibration?
sanskrit_cite:
kartum ity eva yad rūpaṃ jñānādīnāṃ viśeṣaṇam /
karotes tatra ko 'rthaḥ syād yadi saspandatā kila // [AgMsv_1.330]

plain_english: If 'to do' meant vibration, the statement would be that he knows and wants to vibrate; but such vibration cannot belong to an all-pervading self.
sanskrit_cite:
tadāsau spandituṃ vetti prepsatīti bhaved vacaḥ /
tac ca svātmagataṃ nāsya spanditaṃ vaibhavodbhavāt // [AgMsv_1.331]

plain_english: A knowledge without vibration would not be possible even for Śiva, and merely having knowledge, desire, and effort has been described only as an instrument, not as true agency.
sanskrit_cite:
anyad aspanditaṃ jñānaṃ śarvasyāpi na saṃbhavet /
jñānecchāyatnavattvaṃ ca karaṇaṃ tasya bhāṣitam // [AgMsv_1.332]

plain_english: When we analyze the meaning of 'the self is to do', it comes down to knowing, desiring, and striving — even striving to know, to desire, and to strive.
sanskrit_cite:
ātmanaḥ kartum ity asya tato 'rthapravivecane /
jānātīcchan prayatate jñātuṃ yatitum eṣitum // [AgMsv_1.333]

plain_english: Taken one by one, this analysis amounts to knowing to do and wanting to do; that makes one a desirer to act, but not truly an agent.
sanskrit_cite:
pratyekam iti yo 'rthaḥ sa kartuṃ vettīti śabditaḥ /
cikīrṣitṛtvaṃ caitat syān na kartṛtvaṃ punar bhavet // [AgMsv_1.334]

plain_english: If that were so, speech and bodily actions would be wrongly equated with mental ones; or else how could agency in speech and body belong to the same agent?
sanskrit_cite:
tathātve mānasaiḥ sāmyaṃ bhaved vākkāyakarmaṇām /
vākkāyakarmabhir vāsya kathaṃ kartṛtvam āpatet // [AgMsv_1.335]

plain_english: Even if that triad is present, explain how mental actions — and likewise actions arising from mind, speech, and body — can truly belong to him.
sanskrit_cite:
mānasāny api karmāṇi kathaṃ tasyeti gīyatām /
tadguṇatrayasadbhāve manovākkāyasambhuvām // [AgMsv_1.336]

plain_english: If one says the self is the sharer of accumulated actions, that too would be only figurative usage — and that has already been shown to be inadequate.
sanskrit_cite:
karmaṇāṃ saṃciter eṣa karmabhāgīti cen nanu /
upacāro 'yam evaṃ syāt sa cāvastv iti varṇitam // [AgMsv_1.337]

plain_english: Just because qualities such as motion, greatness, and others are present in relation to the self, does that make the self a locus of agency?
sanskrit_cite:
kiṃ cātmagamahattvādidravyāntaguṇasaṃnidhau /
tāni santīti kiṃ so 'pi kartṛtvāyatano bhavet // [AgMsv_1.338]

plain_english: That cannot be accepted, because then agency would arise even in liberation, and the same rule would apply when the qualities of another self are nearby.
sanskrit_cite:
na cāstv ity upagantavyaṃ muktāv api hi tad bhavet /
anyātmaguṇasāṃnidhye samaś caiṣa vidhir yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.339]

plain_english: Then, among selves, there would arise the faults of losing what has been done and gaining what has not been done; and what about the Lord's role in effects everywhere that require intelligence?
sanskrit_cite:
ātmasv ataḥ pravarteran kṛtanāśākṛtāgamāḥ /
kiṃ ceśvareṇa sarvatra buddhimattāvyapekṣiṇi // [AgMsv_1.340]

plain_english: If efficient causality is assigned to the Lord in a complexly arranged effect, what happens when that effect is already fully supplied by its own inherent and other causal factors?
sanskrit_cite:
saṃniveśādhike kārye nimittatvaṃ kṛtaṃ yadi /
svaiḥ svaiś ca samavāyānyakāraṇāṃśaiḥ prapūrite // [AgMsv_1.341]

plain_english: What partial contribution, like that of a potter, could be assigned as the Lord's causality? In the all-doer there is not even the slightest trace of such a partial role.
sanskrit_cite:
kam aṃśaṃ kumbhakārādeḥ prātuṃ bhavatu hetutā /
na hi so 'sty aṃśaleśo 'pi sarvakartari yaṃ prati // [AgMsv_1.342]

plain_english: Agency is nothing other than knowledge, will, and effort; therefore no one else can ever possess true agency.
sanskrit_cite:
na jñānecchāyatnam asti kartṛtvaṃ nānyad ity api /
tasmān nānyasya kartṛtvaṃ kadācid api saṃbhavet // [AgMsv_1.343]

plain_english: The wise understand that the Lord's autonomy is agency; thus, even amid the apparent differences of supreme lords or individual selves, agency is that same autonomy.
sanskrit_cite:
īśvarād īśvarasyāpi svātantryaṃ kartṛtāṃ viduḥ /
tad itthaṃ parameśānāṃ bhede bhede 'pi vātmanām // [AgMsv_1.344]

plain_english: Actions do not bind by their own nature; therefore this good or bad result does not arise merely from that action.
sanskrit_cite:
prabhavanti na karmāṇi bandhanāya svabhāvataḥ /
tasmād idam amuṣmāt syāt karmaṇo vā śubhāśubham // [AgMsv_1.345]

plain_english: That sovereignty belongs to the supreme Lord alone; this has been determined and I have explained it at length elsewhere.
sanskrit_cite:
tad aiśvaryam amuṣyaiva vihitaṃ parameśituḥ /
nirṇītam etad anyatra mayaiva vitataṃ yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.346]

plain_english: Enough of that; returning to the topic, this supreme power of action of the Lord is proclaimed Aghorā because of its non-terrifying nature.
sanskrit_cite:
tad alaṃ prakṛtaṃ brūmaḥ kriyāśaktir iyaṃ parā /
aghoratvena devasya tata eva prakīrtitā // [AgMsv_1.347]

plain_english: Therefore this power is benevolent: for beings who take refuge in Śiva it makes the path direct, and its action is not confined to a limited self.
sanskrit_cite:
dākṣiṇyam ata evāsyā bhāvānāṃ śivasaṃśraye /
yato 'ñjasaiva mārgo 'yaṃ yā kriyā ca na sātmikā // [AgMsv_1.348]

plain_english: One may object that no beings here are established in Śiva-hood as agents; true, but the one being instructed should understand the matter properly.
sanskrit_cite:
nanu nātra sthitāḥ kecid bhāvā ye śivatāśritāḥ /
kartāraḥ satyam itthaṃ tu bodhyamāno 'vadhārayet // [AgMsv_1.349]

plain_english: The Lord of gods is free from constructions of place, time, action, and form; likewise his power is of universal form.
sanskrit_cite:
deśakālakriyākārakalpanāpathavarjitaḥ /
devadevas tathaivāsya śaktiḥ sā viśvarūpiṇī // [AgMsv_1.350]

plain_english: That universe too is free from the stains of time and the rest, abiding in non-difference from Bhairava.
sanskrit_cite:
tad viśvam api kālādikalaṅkāṅkakalojjhitam /
\hspace{3cm} bhairavābhedavartinam // [AgMsv_1.351]

plain_english: By that autonomy it is autonomous, surging forth and abiding within itself; and because it shines, it is never excluded from immersion in Śiva.
sanskrit_cite:
tatsvātantryāt svatantraṃ tat svātmani procchalat sthitam /
yato bhāti tato 'py astaśivāveśabahiṣkṛtam // [AgMsv_1.352]

plain_english: Therefore this supreme power has the form of both Dakṣiṇā and Aghorā, since it will be said to grant beings the fruit of Śiva's abode.
sanskrit_cite:
ata eva parā seyaṃ dakṣiṇāghorarūpiṇī /
yad vakṣyate jantucakre śivadhāmaphalapradāḥ // [AgMsv_1.353]

plain_english: The knowers declare the supreme powers of Śiva to be Aghorā; and elsewhere Śiva's power of action operates within the bound soul.
sanskrit_cite:
parāḥ prakathitās tajjñair aghorāḥ śivaśaktayaḥ /
anyatrāpi kriyāśaktiḥ śivasya paśuvartinī // [AgMsv_1.354]

plain_english: Abiding in its own path it binds, but when known it brings accomplishment; it is proclaimed as the expansion from A to Ha.
sanskrit_cite:
bandhayitrī svamārgasthā jñātā siddhyupapādinī /
akārādihakārāntaḥ prasaro yaḥ pragīyate // [AgMsv_1.355]

plain_english: That same expansion, proceeding from the abode of bindu and taking on non-vowel manifestation, is this unfolding of the power of action as the entire garland of letters.
sanskrit_cite:
sa eva bindunilayād asvaratvam upāśritaḥ /
kriyāśaktivijṛmbheyaṃ samastavarṇamālikā // [AgMsv_1.356]

plain_english: Embraced in the reflective awareness 'I', it abides there; from that arises the vivid flash of the full, supreme I-consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
kroḍīkṛtāv aham iti parāmarśasvarūpiṇī /
tiṣṭhaty eva. tataḥ pūrṇaparāhaṃkārasasphuraḥ // [AgMsv_1.357]

plain_english: It devours the whole mass of bound souls from Ananta to Brahmā and draws the entire moving and unmoving world into the cave of its own belly.
sanskrit_cite:
anantādiviriñcāntapaśusaṃghātaghasmaraḥ /
nijodaradarīnītacarācarajagadvrajaḥ // [AgMsv_1.358]

plain_english: Having swallowed the aggregate of individuals within the reflective awareness of its own consciousness, as long as it flashes forth, it does so by the nature of the power of action.
sanskrit_cite:
svacaitanyavimarśāntar grastapudgalasaṃcayaḥ /
yāvad ullasitas, tāvat kriyāśaktisvarūpataḥ // [AgMsv_1.359]

plain_english: Its state is pervaded by countless unconscious varieties, and its nature is divided into gentle and fierce forms such as endless activity and peace.
sanskrit_cite:
asaṃvijñānaniḥsaṃkhyavaicitryacarcitasthiteḥ /
anantakāryaśāntyādisaumyaraudrabhidātmanaḥ // [AgMsv_1.360]

plain_english: Even though its firm state is revealed by the glory of its own reabsorption, the splendor of Bhairava, by appropriateness, takes on various forms.
sanskrit_cite:
api svagrāsamāhātmyaprakaṭīkṛtasusthiteḥ /
aucityād vividhākārā api bhairavatejasaḥ // [AgMsv_1.361]

plain_english: They are variegated by the recurrence of empty, full, and mixed states, and are solely intent on reabsorbing their own portion, called the universe, into the nature of Śakti.
sanskrit_cite:
riktapūrṇobhayabhavapunarāvṛtticitritāḥ /
śāktasvarūpaviśvākhyasvāṃśagrāsaikalampaṭāḥ // [AgMsv_1.362]

plain_english: Conditioned to uproot states long rooted in world and time, the powers, from their own expansion, send forth each its own mass of rays.
sanskrit_cite:
lokakālacirārūḍhabhāvonmūlanabhāvitāḥ /
śaktayo nijavisphārād raśmipuñjaṃ nijaṃ nijaṃ // [AgMsv_1.363]

plain_english: Spreading forth, and relying on the true state of will, they manifest only what is fitting to them, in a way excluded from worldly left-hand practice.
sanskrit_cite:
prasārayantyaḥ saṃkalpasatyabhāvasamāśrayāt /
svocitāny eva lokotthavāmācārabahiṣkṛteḥ // [AgMsv_1.364]

plain_english: They bring about scriptures that attain fullness, just like the first-arisen teaching in the sphere of transcending the world.
sanskrit_cite:
ghaṭayanty eva śāstrāṇi yātāni paripūrṇatām /
yādṛk prathamasaṃbhūto lokātikrāntigocare // [AgMsv_1.365]

plain_english: That same practice here would be one in which the state of difference is swallowed; this is the full great creation of the supreme Lord, established here.
sanskrit_cite:
samācāraḥ sa evātra grastabhedadaśo bhavet /
pūrṇeyaṃ parameśasya mahāsṛṣṭir iha sthitā // [AgMsv_1.366]

plain_english: In that creation, all the aspects of dissolution and creation exist in the middle; therefore it would not be fitting to call it the very first creation.
sanskrit_cite:
yasyāṃ saṃhārasṛṣṭyaṃśā viśve te madhyavartinaḥ /
sā cādyā sṛṣṭir ity eva naiva vaktuṃ bhavet kṣamam // [AgMsv_1.367]

plain_english: For in a principle beyond place and time, how could there be a first arising and so on? This waking state is the primary one, partaking of the state of unfolding.
sanskrit_cite:
adeśakāle tattve hi katham ādyādisaṃbhavaḥ /
jāgraddaśeyaṃ sā mukhyā pronmeṣapadabhāginī // [AgMsv_1.368]

plain_english: This Brahma is seated on the lotus of awakening of a portion of his own power; these powers unfold beginning from the auspicious Śiva form and extending finally to the form of Brahma.
sanskrit_cite:
brahmaiṣa nijaśaktyaṃśasaṃbodhakamalāsanaḥ /
tā etāḥ sauśivād rūpāt prabhṛti brāhmam antataḥ // [AgMsv_1.369]

plain_english: The powers of the Lord of consciousness unfold by taking form. Even if one might try to say, 'This god is only so much,' such a claim is considered possible.
sanskrit_cite:
rūpaṃ kṛtvā vijṛmbhante saṃvinnāthasya śaktayaḥ /
etāvān eva devo 'yam iti yady api śakyate // [AgMsv_1.370]

plain_english: It cannot truly be said, because the great Lord, whose nature is consciousness, is immeasurable. I have stated this clearly in the Prabodhapañcadaśikā.
sanskrit_cite:
na vaktum aprameyatvāc cidrūpasya maheśituḥ /
prabodhapañcadaśikāmadhye tādṛṅ mayā sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.371]

plain_english: It has been said that limited manifestation is indeed the characteristic of the inert; awareness is distinct from the inert because it is not measured.
sanskrit_cite:
uktaṃ mitaprakāśatvaṃ jaḍasya kila lakṣaṇam /
jaḍād vilakṣaṇo bodho yato na parimīyate // [AgMsv_1.372]

plain_english: Even so, the god, who is himself beyond measure, by the exercise of his own freedom makes himself into the moving and unmoving universe.
sanskrit_cite:
tathāpi svayam etādṛg devo mānavivarjitaḥ /
nijasvātantryayogena kṛtvātmānaṃ carācaram // [AgMsv_1.373]

plain_english: Through Īśa, Tatpuruṣa, and Aja, in their arisen and about-to-arise forms, combining as single ones, as six, as one, as a triad, and as three dyads,
sanskrit_cite:
īśatatpuruṣājātair udbhūtair udbubhūṣubhiḥ /
ekakaiḥ ṣaḍbhir, ekena trikeṇa, dvyātmakais tribhiḥ // [AgMsv_1.374]

plain_english: There arises a manifold state of the ten divisions of Śiva; indeed, this is due to the mixture of varied consciousnesses.
sanskrit_cite:
jāyate śivabhedānāṃ daśānāṃ vividhā sthitiḥ /
ata eva vicitrābhyaḥ saṃvidbhyo miśratāvaśāt // [AgMsv_1.375]

plain_english: Even in what is called Śiva, varied knowledges of difference were unfolded when the left and right aspects of the three faces came together.
sanskrit_cite:
citrāṇy atra śivākhye 'pi bhedajñānāni tenire /
yadā trayāṇāṃ vaktrāṇāṃ vāmadakṣiṇasaṃgatiḥ // [AgMsv_1.376]

plain_english: Then, as each becomes a distinct power through the future, present, and arisen modes, the six in a triad make the Rudra division established in eighteen forms.
sanskrit_cite:
tadā pratyekaśaktitvaṃ bhaviṣyadbhavadudbhavaiḥ /
ṣaṇṇāṃ tritve rudrabhedas tenāṣṭādaśadhā sthitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.377]

plain_english: Since each is declared to be five-faced, what is divided into ten and eighteen becomes innumerable through further divisions.
sanskrit_cite:
ekaikaṃ pañcavaktraṃ ca vaktraṃ yasmāt pragīyate /
daśāṣṭādaśabhinnasya tato bhedair asaṃkhyatā // [AgMsv_1.378]

plain_english: Because in them the distinctions are determined by each one's own knowledge and action as stated before, there is no mere repetition.
sanskrit_cite:
pūrvoditayathāsvasvajñānakarmavicitritāḥ /
nirṇīyante yatas teṣu tena no punaruktatā // [AgMsv_1.379]

plain_english: For awareness, practice, and the sequence of action are indeed different in each case, as declared there; yet all of them lead to the abode of Śiva.
sanskrit_cite:
anyānya eva bodho hi samācāraḥ kriyākramaḥ /
tatra tatra tathā proktaḥ sarvas tu śivadhāmagaḥ // [AgMsv_1.380]

plain_english: Just as all drops of water come to rest in the great ocean, so all knowledges and actions come to rest in the great Lord, the ocean of consciousness.
sanskrit_cite:
yathā jalakaṇāh sarve viśrāmyanti mahāmbudhau /
tathā jñānakriyāḥ sarvāḥ saṃvitsindhau maheśvare // [AgMsv_1.381]

plain_english: Even limited water on earth is drawn up by the sun's rays and returns again to the great ocean through rain; so too, all knowledge and action in the world, some arising by themselves and some through others in succession, sink into the ocean of Śiva.
sanskrit_cite:
mitam api jalaṃ bhūmau sūryāṃśubhiḥ kila pīyate / tad api ca punar vṛṣṭidvāraiḥ prayāti mahārṇavam /
jagati nikhilaṃ jñānaṃ karma sphuṭaṃ kim api svayaṃ / kim api ca paraiḥ pāramparyāc chivārṇasi majjati // [AgMsv_1.382]

plain_english: And that heart-mark at the right end, regarded as the supreme heart, is also fully filled with all created beings taken within it.
sanskrit_cite:
yac cānte dakṣiṇe hārdaṃ liṅgaṃ hṛt paramaṃ matam /
tad apy antaḥkṛtāśeṣasṛṣṭabhāvasunirbharam // [AgMsv_1.383]

plain_english: And because it devours the rays of māyā that produce difference, that, as the dissolver of all, is dark and bears the form of darkness.
sanskrit_cite:
bhedabhāvakamāyīyatejoṃśagrasanāc ca tat /
sarvasaṃhārakatvena kṛṣṇaṃ timirarūpadhṛt // [AgMsv_1.384]

plain_english: Therefore it is stated in the Vijñānaśāstra by the great Lord: 'All space is dissolved in the head,' and so forth, referring to the darkness of the Lord.
sanskrit_cite:
vijñānaśāstre kathitam ata eva maheśinā /
līnaṃ mūrdhni viyat sarvam ityādi timiraṃ vibhoḥ // [AgMsv_1.385]

plain_english: Thus, on a dark night at the arrival of the dark fortnight, one should contemplate for a long time the Bhairava form, which is hard to name, by those who practice contemplation.
sanskrit_cite:
evam eva durniśāyāṃ kṛṣṇapakṣāgame ciram /
bhāvayed bhairavaṃ rūpaṃ bhāvayadbhir durābhidam // [AgMsv_1.386]

plain_english: And it is said: where light, suffering, and darkness are covered by nonduality, there is no connection with ignorance and karma, because dependence and the like are not seen.
sanskrit_cite:
uktaṃ ca yatra svar duḥkhaṃ tamo vādvayasaṃvṛte /
nāvidyākarmasaṃbandhaḥ pāratantryādidarśanāt // [AgMsv_1.387]

plain_english: Therefore, in this Bhairava body of the form of darkness, the group of four faces shines fully by being inwardly dissolved.
sanskrit_cite:
tad atra timirākāre bhairavīye vapuṣy alam /
antarlīnatayā bhāti yāvad vaktracatuṣṭayam // [AgMsv_1.388]

plain_english: As about to emerge, emerged, about to withdraw, and withdrawn, this division therefore becomes simultaneously sixteenfold.
sanskrit_cite:
udbubhūṣu tathodbhūtaṃ tirodhitsu tirohitam /
tato yugapad evaitadbhidā ṣoḍaśakātmakam // [AgMsv_1.389]

plain_english: Entering the right, emissive, heart, and autonomous aspects in Śiva, the scripture named Bhairava becomes simultaneously an eight-times-eight system.
sanskrit_cite:
dakṣe vaisargike hārde svatantre ca śive viśat /
aṣṭāṣṭakātmakaṃ śāstraṃ yugapad bhairavābhidham // [AgMsv_1.390]

plain_english: Thus the scripture, named Rudra, Shiva, and Bhairava, is established as threefold in reality; for indeed this being of knowledge unfolds in a threefold way.
sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ tantraṃ rudraśivabhairavākhyaṃ sthitaṃ tridhā /
vastuto hi tridhaiveyaṃ jñānasattā vijṛmbhate // [AgMsv_1.391]

plain_english: It unfolds by difference, by difference-and-nondifference, and by the full junction of nondifference; and likewise there are three principal powers of Shambhu, beginning with will.
sanskrit_cite:
bhedena bhedābhedena pūrṇenābhedasandhinā /
tathā ca mukhyāḥ śāmbhavyas tisra icchādiśaktayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.392]

plain_english: There indeed, by elaboration, there is the application of the five powers and so on; thus, though divided in the middle, that triad is indeed supreme.
sanskrit_cite:
tatraiva tu prapañcena pañcaśaktyādiyojanam /
itthaṃ madhye vibhinnaṃ tat trikam eva paraṃ tathā // [AgMsv_1.393]

plain_english: The scripture is established in our teacher's house through the lineage sequence; therefore, indeed, because of its nearness to the left and right scriptures.
sanskrit_cite:
śāstram asmadgurugṛhe saṃpradāyakramāt sthitam /
ata eva hi naikaṭyād vāmadakṣiṇaśāstrayoḥ // [AgMsv_1.394]

plain_english: The Kaula stream fully unfolds at the edge of the edge-stream; and from that, full with all the limiting conditions of beings withdrawn.
sanskrit_cite:
dhārā prāntadharāprānte kaulikī pravijṛmbhate /
tato 'pi saṃhṛtāśeṣabhāvopādhisunirbharaḥ // [AgMsv_1.395]

plain_english: Bhairava, whose activity is expanded by the rising fluid of supreme reality, embraces the triad of powers in sequence in those Ishana, left, and right channels, from Apara up to Para, and abides.
sanskrit_cite:
bhairavaḥ paramārthodyadravabṛmhitavṛttikaḥ /
īśānavāmadakṣāsu tāsu śaktitrayaṃ kramāt /
aparādiparāprāntaṃ kroḍīkṛtyāvatiṣṭhate // [AgMsv_1.396]

plain_english: It manifests that division of difference and makes it clear; and then they declare that infinite, reabsorbing form of the supreme lord to be, in reality, truly three-headed.
sanskrit_cite:
tad vibhāvayati bhedavibhāgaṃ tatsphuṭatvakṛd atho tam anantam /
saṃgrasiṣṇu parameśvararūpaṃ vastutas triśira eva nirāhuḥ // [AgMsv_1.397]

plain_english: The upper, left, and other tantras and kulas are established in that stream for the removal of the contraction of difference.
sanskrit_cite:
ūrdhvavāmatadanyāni tantrāṇi ca kulāni ca /
rūḍhāny amuṣyāṃ dhārāyāṃ bhedasaṃkocahānaye // [AgMsv_1.398]

plain_english: The triad-meaning, established threefold in supreme light, is uttered by the supreme lord as the knowledge-moon.
sanskrit_cite:
paraprakāśaviṣayas trikārthas traidham āsthitaḥ /
sa eṣa parameśena jñānacandrākhyayoditaḥ // [AgMsv_1.399]

plain_english: All scripture-meaning rests in the course of supreme speech, without unfolded distinctions of meaning and word.
sanskrit_cite:
sa eva sarvaḥ śāstrārthaḥ paravāgvṛttisaṃśritaḥ /
anullasitatadvācyavācakādivibhaktikaḥ // [AgMsv_1.400]

plain_english: Afterward, in the self where knowledge-power dominates, action-power remains very subtle within sadākhya lordship.
sanskrit_cite:
paścāt tu jñānaśaktyaṃśaprādhānyasphuritātmani /
kriyāśaktau susūkṣmāyāṃ sādākhyaiśvaryasaṃpadi // [AgMsv_1.401]

plain_english: In the paśyantī and madhyamā abodes, through the mention of stirring, it exists as word and sentence in letter form.
sanskrit_cite:
paśyantīmadhyamādhāmni sañjalpollekhayogataḥ /
padavākyasvarūpeṇa vartate varṇarūpiṇā // [AgMsv_1.402]

plain_english: In the Svacchanda scripture it is said that Sadāśiva himself joined the tantra with prior and later words and sentences.
sanskrit_cite:
svacchandaśāstre tenoktaṃ svayaṃ devaḥ sadāśivaḥ /
pūrvottarapadair vākyais tantraṃ yojitavān iti // [AgMsv_1.403]

plain_english: Thus it is also said there: in that sushiva covering on the path, Sadāśiva is first to be known.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā ca tatraivoktaṃ tatsuśivāvaraṇe 'dhvani /
suśivāvaraṇaṃ pūrvaṃ tatra jñeyaḥ sadāśivaḥ // [AgMsv_1.404]

plain_english: Joined with ten Śiva and endowed with eighteen Rudra, authority is in the Īśa principle, but the desire to grasp that is in Sauśiva.
sanskrit_cite:
śivadaśakasaṃyukto rudrāṣṭādaśakānvitaḥ /
adhikāro hīśatattve tajjighṛkṣā tu sauśive // [AgMsv_1.405]

plain_english: In the covering, from bindu in the enjoyment-abode, from the lord's abundance, there is a supreme triad of Bhairava knowledge in the power principle.
sanskrit_cite:
varaṇe binduto bhogadhāmni vibhavato vibhoḥ /
bhairavākhyasya bodhasya śaktitattve paraṃ trayam // [AgMsv_1.406]

plain_english: Therefore the position is above Īśvara and below the Sadāśiva station, as said by the sushiva covering in the glorious Svacchanda scripture.
sanskrit_cite:
sthitis tasmād īśvarordhve sadāśivapadād adhaḥ /
suśivāvaraṇenoktā śrīmatsvacchandaśāsane // [AgMsv_1.407]

plain_english: After that, in these Śiva-Rudra distinctions, enough; on the māyīya path, established by the Śivas, the one named Śiva is said.
sanskrit_cite:
tadanantaram etāsu śivarudrabhidāsv alam /
māyīyādhvani kḷptāsu śivair uktaḥ śivābhidhaḥ // [AgMsv_1.408]

plain_english: The difference, by Rudras and called Rudra, thus reaches variety; then, from the flourishing essence of rising action, it becomes gradually clear.
sanskrit_cite:
bhedo rudraiś ca rudrākhya iti prāpto vicitratām /
tataḥ prodyatkriyāsāraprollāsāt kramaśaḥ sphuṭam // [AgMsv_1.409]

plain_english: The scriptural meanings that rest on Maya-born Vaikhari speech heard by all, and whose nature is letters, sentences, and words, are within the range of the world.
sanskrit_cite:
sarvagocaramāyīyaśrutavaikharyupāśritāḥ /
varṇavākyapadātmānaḥ śāstrārthā lokagocarāḥ // [AgMsv_1.410]

plain_english: Having resorted to those various transmitters of the tantras, they proceed; therefore, at first, as long as they come through the Maya-born cavity of Vaikhari.
sanskrit_cite:
samāśritya pravartante tāṃs tāṃs tantrāvatārakān /
tena prathamato yāvan māyīyāṃ vaikharīṃ darīm // [AgMsv_1.411]

plain_english: This scriptural meaning, bound by Maya-born letters, has not arrived within as that which consists of the supreme speech-letters of essential awakening.
sanskrit_cite:
māyīyavarṇasaṃdṛbdhaḥ śāstrārtho nāyam āgataḥ /
antaḥ sāravibodhaikaparavāṅmayavarṇakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.412]

plain_english: The scriptural meaning, refined by the root impression of uncontrived supreme immersion, extends to the worldly level, yet it is in the supreme thirty-seventh lord.
sanskrit_cite:
akṛtrimaparāveśamūlasaṃskārasaṃskṛtaḥ /
śāstrārtho laukikānto 'sti saptatriṃśe pare vibhau // [AgMsv_1.413]

plain_english: For there, unreal beings have no reality anywhere at all; how could respect arise in a lordly nature overcome by disrespect?
sanskrit_cite:
tatrāsatāṃ hi bhāvānāṃ kvāpi nāsty eva satyatā /
svāminy avinayākrāntaprakṛtau vinayaḥ kutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.414]

plain_english: Therefore the entire meaning of scripture is established as the nature of the supreme principle; hence even these Vedas and others are Maya-born portions of teaching.
sanskrit_cite:
tasmāt samastaśāstrārthaḥ paratattvātmanā sthitaḥ /
ato vedādayo 'py ete māyīyāḥ śāsanāṃśavaḥ // [AgMsv_1.415]

plain_english: They shine forth from the power of the Bhairava-sun alone, not from elsewhere; for apart from the reflective awareness of consciousness there could be no other cause anywhere at all.
sanskrit_cite:
sphuranti bhairavādityaprabhāvād eva nānyataḥ /
na hi saṃvidvimarśāt syād anyat kvāpy eva kāraṇam // [AgMsv_1.416]

plain_english: The consciousness of the lord of consciousness would be consciousness alone; therefore, since it is spoken of as both effect and cause, that status is applied only figuratively.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃvinnāthasya saṃvit syāt saṃvid eva tathā yataḥ /
kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ ceti tathātva upacāryate // [AgMsv_1.417]

plain_english: For in the sequential transformation of a being with extended properties, at the beginning and at the end, consciousness alone appears as its very form.
sanskrit_cite:
pariṇāme hi bhāvasya kramād vitatadharmaṇaḥ /
ādyantayoḥ saṃvid eva rūpatvenāvabhāsate // [AgMsv_1.418]

plain_english: And if consciousness could endure division by time, then we would clearly be enjoying gravel bits of sky cut by a sharpened sword.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃvic ca kālakalanāṃ saheta yadi tat sphuṭam /
bhuñjīmahi niśātāsicchinnā vyomāṃśaśarkarāḥ // [AgMsv_1.419]

plain_english: Therefore all the scriptures, because they do not fall away from the form of consciousness and because consciousness is self-luminous, are in reality self-luminous.
sanskrit_cite:
ataḥ samagraśāstrāṇi saṃvidrūpāparicyuteḥ /
saṃvidaḥ svaprakāśatvāt svaprakāśāni vastutaḥ // [AgMsv_1.420]

plain_english: And it should not be said that the expressed ever stands apart from the expresser; for by autonomy the expresser alone appears as what will be expressed.
sanskrit_cite:
na ca vācyaṃ pṛthag jātu vācakād vyavatiṣṭhate /
svātantryād abhidhātaiva bhāvivācyatayā yataḥ // [AgMsv_1.421]

plain_english: Sometimes the expressing aspect appears with the expressed absorbed into its own nature; sometimes, instead, it appears as expressing a general flash.
sanskrit_cite:
kadācid vācakāṃśas tu svarūpagrastavācyakaḥ /
nirbhāsate kadācit tu sāmānyollāsavācakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.422]

plain_english: Sometimes it shines, qualified by near and countless qualifiers, with a surge of the clear expressed aspect of its own form.
sanskrit_cite:
jātucin nikaṭānantaviśeṣaṇaviśeṣitaḥ /
sphuṭasvarūpavācyāṃśasamudrekeṇa bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.423]

plain_english: Therefore sometimes there is orientation toward meaning, and likewise sometimes orientation toward the word's own form; sometimes a state in which the meaning is desired to be known, and sometimes a state consisting of rasa.
sanskrit_cite:
tenārthaparatā jātu svarūpaparatā tathā /
bubhūtsitārthā kvāpi kvacid rasamayī daśā // [AgMsv_1.424]

plain_english: A variegated state of words is observed, because they do not depart from the form of consciousness; since it flashes through the varied flashings of consciousness, what is wonderful about that?
sanskrit_cite:
śabdānāṃ lakṣyate citrā saṃvidrūpānapāyataḥ /
saṃvidvicitrakacanaiḥ kacatīti kim adbhutam // [AgMsv_1.425]

plain_english: Thus word, non-different from the Śiva-natured level of reflective awareness, becomes clear here and illuminates both itself and other. Valid cognition is nothing but reflective awareness whose essence is consciousness; anything else is called cognition only by figurative extension from that.
sanskrit_cite:
itthaṃ śivātmakavimarśapadād abhinnaḥ śabdaḥ sphuṭatvata iha svaparaprakāśaḥ /
mānaṃ tad eva citisāravimarśamātram anyat punas tadupacāravaśāt tathā hi // [AgMsv_1.426]

plain_english: That ultimate consciousness, whose nature is self-luminous, is called self-awareness, because the ordering of the entire universe rests on it.
sanskrit_cite:
svaprakāśātmikā yeyaṃ saṃvittiḥ pāramārthikī /
tat svasaṃvedanaṃ proktaṃ yato viśvavyavasthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.427]

plain_english: This consciousness never goes beyond a nature whose very self is reflective awareness. Its reflective awareness is its supreme, full enjoyment, and that state is called paśyantī.
sanskrit_cite:
sā caiṣā na vimarśātmasvarūpam ativartate /
vimarśo 'syāḥ paro bhogaḥ pūrṇaḥ paśyanty udāhṛtā // [AgMsv_1.428]

plain_english: Understand that same goddess as parāparā, which is valid cognition. In that state the knowable object appears on the lower side and stands forth through identity with that cognition.
sanskrit_cite:
parāparā saiva devī mānam ity avadhāryatām /
yatrāparāṃśagaṃ meyaṃ tādātmyād vyavatiṣṭhate // [AgMsv_1.429]

plain_english: For an object cannot be determined by a cognition that is entirely different from it; just as a crow cannot claim the whiteness that belongs to a swan.
sanskrit_cite:
na hi bhinnena mānena meyasya syād vyavastitiḥ /
na hi haṃsasya śuklatve kākaḥ śvetatvam arhati // [AgMsv_1.430]

plain_english: The teacher Śaṅkaranandana says the same thing: establishment does not arise merely because something is cognition, nor because it is other than cognition, nor because of sublation, nor because of non-establishment.
sanskrit_cite:
etad eva tathā cāha guruḥ śaṅkaranandanaḥ /
na mānatvāt tato 'nyatvān na bādhād asthiteḥ sthitiḥ // [AgMsv_1.431]

plain_english: A thing is established through properties that are inseparable from luminosity and fixed in existence; if it stood outside that, it could not attain establishment at all.
sanskrit_cite:
prakāśenāvinābhūtaiḥ sattāyāṃ niyatātmabhiḥ /
dharmair bhāvo bahirbhāvān na bhāvaḥ siddhim ṛcchati // [AgMsv_1.432]

plain_english: Therefore the triad of knower, cognition, and known, though appearing in those roles, is in essence nothing but consciousness and shines by its own nature as self-luminous.
sanskrit_cite:
tena saṃvittikātmaiva mātṛmānaprameyatā /
gṛhṇatī svaprakāśatvaṃ svabhāvād eva bhāsate // [AgMsv_1.433]

plain_english: That consciousness, inwardly beautiful with mantra-natured verbal reflective awareness, is valid by itself, because it does not depend on anything else.
sanskrit_cite:
sā cāntaḥsthitamantrātmaśabdanāmarśasundarā /
anapekṣānyavirahāt pramāṇaṃ svata eva hi // [AgMsv_1.434]

plain_english: The various names of that same consciousness, arising in many modes from its own grace, were fashioned by different theorists.
sanskrit_cite:
tasyā eva vicitrāṇi nāmāni bahubhaṅgibhiḥ /
tatprasādotthitāny eva vādinaḥ paryacīkḷpan // [AgMsv_1.435]

plain_english: And so the teaching that perception rests on the sphere of the eye and other senses is now examined.
sanskrit_cite:
tathā ca cakṣurādyakṣamaṇḍalīṭaṅkaniṣṭhitam /
pratyakṣam iti yad gītaṃ tat tāvat pravivicyate // [AgMsv_1.436]

plain_english: If the senses cannot be established apart from consciousness, then the supposed identity of object and cognition would have to be treated like that of an external pot and so on.
sanskrit_cite:
saṃvittivyatirekeṇa yady akṣāṇāṃ vyavasthitiḥ /
na syād arthapramāṇaikyaṃ tarhi bāhyaghaṭādivat // [AgMsv_1.437]

plain_english: An objection says: the eye and other senses are instruments of the self, unlike a pot and so on; therefore things are cognized by those senses, not by pots and the like.
sanskrit_cite:
nanv ātmanaś cakṣurādi karaṇaṃ na ghaṭādikam /
tasmāt tenaiva bhāvānāṃ mānaṃ na tu ghaṭādibhiḥ // [AgMsv_1.438]

plain_english: If the self is taken as all-pervading, its contact is undifferentiated; and since the eye and other senses are not relevantly different in materiality from pots and the like, mere contact cannot explain their special role.
sanskrit_cite:
vyāpakābhimatasyāsya saṃyoge cāviśeṣiṇaḥ /
bhautikatvāviśeṣeṇa ghaṭādyaiś cakṣurādinā // [AgMsv_1.439]

plain_english: How could the self's need for an instrument be fulfilled in a determinate way? Only a specific contact, not a generic one, could be the basis for something becoming an instrument.
sanskrit_cite:
ātmanaḥ karaṇākāṅkṣāpūraṇaṃ niyataṃ kutaḥ /
viśiṣṭa eva saṃyogaḥ karaṇatve nibandhanam // [AgMsv_1.440]

plain_english: If one says the specific difference comes from various actions called merit and demerit, that explanation is devoid of the appearance of genuine reasoning.
sanskrit_cite:
viśeṣaḥ karmabhis tais tair dharmādharmagiroditaiḥ /
tad etad yuktisadbhāvapratibhāvikalātmakaḥ // [AgMsv_1.441]

plain_english: One who, intent on evasion, speaks of cognition as arising from an all-pervading self in contact with all the senses deceives the deluded.
sanskrit_cite:
bruvan vañcayate mugdhān palāyanaparāyaṇaḥ /
yac cāśeṣākṣasaṃyogivyāpakātmavaśotthitām // [AgMsv_1.442]

plain_english: Mind is said to cut cognition at once; even there, mind-self alone is first fitted.
sanskrit_cite:
yugapaj jñaptim ācchettuṃ mano nāma nigadyate /
tatrāpi brumahe pūrvaṃ manasātmaiva yujyate // [AgMsv_1.443]

plain_english: Who would make self-mind union? If it is pervasive, all minds would go.
sanskrit_cite:
tatrāpy ātmamanoyogaṃ kaḥ kuryād iti carcyatām /
vyāpakatvād asau syāc cet sarvair eva mano vrajet // [AgMsv_1.444]

plain_english: If one union arises, all would become omniscient, if own mind depends on presiding senses.
sanskrit_cite:
ekasya jāte saṃyoge sarvaḥ sarvajñatām iyāt /
yadi svāntam adhiṣṭhātṛ cakṣurādyam apekṣate // [AgMsv_1.445]

plain_english: Therefore presiding over objects is so many along the sense-particle path, illuminated by contact with fine sense particles.
sanskrit_cite:
tenādhiṣṭhānam arthānāṃ tāvato 'kṣāṃśavartmanaḥ /
akṣādhiṣṭhitasūkṣmāṃśabhāgasaṃparkabhāsitaḥ // [AgMsv_1.446]

plain_english: Let one atom of an external object like a pot appear; but if mind-presiding arises in sense-range.
sanskrit_cite:
bāhyasyārthasya kuṇḍāder aṇur eko 'vabhāsatām /
athāpi mānasādhiṣṭhā jātā ced akṣagocare // [AgMsv_1.447]

plain_english: Power arises in its own domain; then eye-rays are emitted from the tiniest hole.
sanskrit_cite:
tad etasya svaviṣaye śaktataivopajāyate /
tarhi sūkṣmatamacchidranissṛtā netraraśmayaḥ // [AgMsv_1.448]

plain_english: In the world-abiding flood they do not make valid cognition; senses grasp beings situated in a suitable place.
sanskrit_cite:
viśvavartini bhāvaughe na pramāṃ kurvate kutaḥ /
yogyadeśasthitān bhāvān gṛhṇate 'kṣāṇi nanv alam // [AgMsv_1.449]

plain_english: Suitability of place is to be examined; the place where cognition occurs is called suitable.
sanskrit_cite:
yogyataiva hi deśasya kīdṛśīti vicāryatām /
yatrasthasya bhaved vittiḥ sa deśo yogya ucyate // [AgMsv_1.450]

plain_english: Where would cognition occur? It is not shown; these logician-pretenders lack reasoned presentation.
sanskrit_cite:
kutrasthasya bhaved vittir iti kiṃ vā na darśyate /
tad amī tārkikammanyā yuktyupanyāsavarjitāḥ // [AgMsv_1.451]
